title: Paffett wins as Mercedes bounces back at the Lausitzring
dek: Gary Paffett passed pole-sitter Christian Vietoris at the first corner and won by 6.8 seconds from Mike Rockenfeller, whose second place put him level with Bruno Spengler at the top of the standings.

chapters.title: Spengler's lead is narrow after Austria
text: The fourth race of the 2013 DTM, at the Lausitzring on Sunday 16 June, came two weeks after BMW had swept the podium at the Red Bull Ring. Bruno Spengler won there from pole, and the result took him to the top of the standings on 53 points, 12 clear of Mike Rockenfeller, who had arrived in Austria as the leader and left it second on 41. Augusto Farfus was third on 33 and Marco Wittmann, who had finished second for the new BMW Team MTEK, fourth on 32.

Mercedes had yet to win in 2013, and its best finisher in Austria had been Christian Vietoris in seventh. Gary Paffett had only 22 points after three rounds. Audi, meanwhile, started the weekend strongly: on Saturday morning Jamie Green of Abt Sportsline headed Paffett in the practice session, and Audi drivers held the top spot for 80 of its 90 minutes.

Hankook's new option tyre was again the strategic variable. It gave faster lap times for a limited number of laps before dropping off, and the choice of when to fit it had decided much of the racing so far. After Spengler's late-stop win in Austria, the question was whether a rival could find a similar edge.

chapters.title: Vietoris takes a maiden pole for Mercedes
text: Christian Vietoris took the first pole of his DTM career with a 1:17.715 in the single-lap final session, 0.225 seconds clear of his HWA team-mate Paffett, in second. It put Mercedes back on pole and gave HWA three cars in the top four.

Green was third on 1:18.028, his best qualifying result since joining Audi, with Robert Wickens fourth for HWA despite a mistake on his final lap. None of the BMWs reached the last session: Spengler was the best of them in fifth, on the third row alongside Rockenfeller in sixth, and Adrien Tambay and Edoardo Mortara followed in seventh and eighth. Roberto Merhi was ninth.

The grid then shifted. Farfus, who had qualified tenth, was given a five-place penalty for using a set of tyres not allocated to him in morning practice and started 15th, and Timo Glock took a three-place penalty for impeding Daniel Juncadella on a flying lap and started 17th. Timo Scheider and Mattias Ekström were knocked out in the first session and started 16th and 18th, while Martin Tomczyk, who parked early with a broken splitter, was on the back row in 22nd, behind Andy Priaulx and Joey Hand.

chapters.title: Paffett takes the lead at Turn 1
text: Paffett got the better of Vietoris on the run to the first corner and led the field out of it, then pulled out an advantage of nearly three seconds before his first stop. Rockenfeller, who had been sixth on the first lap, had started on standard tyres and went for the options as the pit window opened on lap three, a move that would shape the whole race.

Wickens ran with Rockenfeller as the pair stretched their option stints, and by the time everyone had made a first stop they held second and third. Several of the front-runners started on the option compound, while others, Rockenfeller among them, began on the standard tyre and switched early to make up ground.

chapters.title: Rockenfeller closes, Paffett pulls away
text: Paffett pitted from the lead, changing from soft options to the harder standard tyre, and rejoined with Rockenfeller on his tail rather than Vietoris. The Audi driver ran a 39-lap stint on the options, longer than any of the other contenders, and made up time on them, but on the standard tyre in the final laps he could not hold the pace and ceded about seven seconds to Paffett over the last ten laps.

Paffett said afterwards that he had used the options hard to pull a gap after the start, and that the car's pace on the standard tyres in qualifying had been the key. Wickens stayed ahead of Rockenfeller until being passed at Turn 1 on lap 25, took a short middle stint and a second set of standards, and fell back from the fight.

Lower down the field, Ekström made both of his mandatory stops inside the first ten laps, ran a 43-lap stint on options and passed Tambay, Pascal Wehrlein and Mortara in the final ten laps to climb from 18th on the grid to eighth.

chapters.title: Paffett wins by 6.8s; Spengler holds off Ekström by 0.029s
text: Paffett took the flag after 52 laps in 1:09:58.562, 6.800 seconds ahead of Rockenfeller, who set the fastest lap of the race, a 1:18.268 on lap seven. Vietoris completed the podium, 11.510 seconds behind, after passing his team-mate Wickens in the closing stages.

Wickens was fourth, 12.790 seconds back, and Green took fifth for Abt, 14.138 seconds behind the winner. Juncadella made up seven places from 13th on the grid to sixth, with his best move coming late on when he passed Spengler into Turn 1.

Spengler, who started fifth, was caught by Juncadella late on and finished seventh, 21.592 seconds behind, with Ekström crossing the line just 0.029 seconds behind him. Mortara was ninth, Merhi tenth, and Wittmann and Priaulx were the only two cars a lap down, classified 21st and 22nd.

chapters.title: Rockenfeller and Spengler level on 59
text: Paffett said the car had been superb and the race perfect. He said he had wrung everything out of the option tyres and then tried to keep his lead big enough to stop Rockenfeller using DRS on the standards. It was his first win of the season and gave Mercedes its first win of 2013.

Rockenfeller said the early switch to the option tyre had worked very well after the standard tyre cost him a little time at the start, and that he would have liked a few more laps on it, but that the team had changed back to the standard for safety after such a long stint. He said starting sixth and finishing second meant they had taken the maximum out of the day.

The result left Rockenfeller and Spengler level on 59 points, with Rockenfeller ahead on countback because of his better results: Rockenfeller had scored 18 for second to add to his 41 from the first three rounds, while Spengler had added only six for seventh. Paffett climbed to 47 points in third, and Vietoris, who took his second podium of the season after passing Wickens in the closing laps, moved to fourth on 40. Farfus and Wittmann stayed on 33 and 32. Green, who started third, finished fifth for Abt Sportsline, while Juncadella's climb from 13th to sixth was one of the drives of the day.

For BMW it was a sobering weekend after the Red Bull Ring: Spengler's seventh was the only finish in the points for the marque, and none of the BMWs had reached the final qualifying session. Mercedes, with three cars in the first four places in qualifying and in the race, had pulled itself back into the championship fight. The next race is the Norisring on 14 July.

facts.v: Gary Paffett won over 52 laps in 1:09:58.562, 6.800 seconds ahead of Mike Rockenfeller, after passing pole-sitter Vietoris at the first corner.
